text: A1 and A2 give incompatible exact results: A2 adds unmatched .al paths to A1's test, which asserts exactly two diagnostics.
evidence: A2 is now its own test, al_looking_paths_stay_unmatched, with an exact list of two and exit 2. A1 asserts its own exact list of four.

text: Rename semantics were unproved (AL→non-AL and non-AL→AL, hunked and hunkless), and AL→non-AL (Foo.al→Foo.al.bak) would read as 'not AL' although AL source left.
evidence: Design: an AL→non-AL rename gives diff-file-deleted on old_path; non-AL→AL is handled as today. A3 (d) covers a hunked .al→.json rename and (e) a hunkless .json→.al rename onto an existing workspace file.

text: Only-in paths carry no file/folder information: a new folder (Only in ./src: NewFeature) would be labelled not-AL although it may hold AL files, and a folder named x.al would read as AL.
evidence: An Only-in path is diff-file-not-al only when it is not AL-looking AND no workspace file key lies below it under any reading; otherwise today's handling applies (A3 (c)). Stated limit: the rule classifies AL-LOOKING paths, and the x.al folder reads as AL. The old tree is not probed.

text: DRY: source_text::has_al_extension already is this check, and workspace discovery uses it; a new is_al_path would drift from it (e.g. on a segment named '.al').
evidence: The Rule uses crate::source_text::has_al_extension(Path::new(path)), so no new helper is written.

text: Edge coverage was incomplete: permission-set .xml, extensionless paths, mixed-case .Al.
evidence: A1 adds permissions.xml and LICENSE (no extension). A2 adds src/Other.Al with a case-sensitivity mutation. Trailing slash: Path::extension ignores a trailing '/', and diff records carry none; no new behaviour.

text: Promised invariants had no proof: non-AL-only input (exit 2), a malformed non-AL hunk, a user-named non-AL --file, and mixed-diff entries equal to the AL-only baseline.
evidence: A4 (a)/(b)/(c) are CLI cases. A1 compares entries with the AL-only run. The Design says a rejected-header non-AL file keeps its diff-parse-error as well.

text: Local goldens cannot prove CentralGauge accepts 1.8.0; consumer readiness must gate the rollout, and the demo version should be stated.
evidence: Design 'Rollout': merging to master releases nothing. The 10-27 demo runs on the released v2.1.1 (digest 1.7.0). A release that ships 1.8.0 waits on CentralGauge's ALSEM_SCHEMAS listing 1.8.0, tracked by discovery D1. The CHANGELOG says so, and release tags are operator-controlled.

text: 'An AL path the workspace cannot match' understates diff-file-unmatched, which also covers a workspace file with no routine.
evidence: The meaning is now 'an AL-looking path that resolves no routine-bearing workspace file' (:343-368), including an Only-in folder of workspace files. The CHANGELOG and the contract line use it.

text: Binary and mode-only diff --git sections produce no record, so 'dropping would hide input' overstates the rationale.
evidence: Stated limits: those sections give no diagnostic either way, and the rationale is now 'no parsed record is dropped'.

text: The human unit test pins rendering only, and its count was wrong ('9 lines'; it is 11, becoming 12).
evidence: A4 says 12 lines and that it proves rendering. A1's CLI --format human assertion proves the use.

evidence: There are two guards sharing has_al_extension: one at the top of the parsed.files loop, covering deleted and other records, and one in the Only-in loop. diff_key is unchanged.

evidence: Guard 2 now says the readings are built as diff_readings builds them (:311-317) but taken before its filter (:318-322). A3 (c) fails if this is done wrong.

text: The AL→non-AL arm fires on any record with an old_path, but the parser also sets old_path on a Modified record whose ---/+++ paths differ (a git copy, or GNU diff -u x.al x.al.bak), so a copy reads as a deletion of source that still exists.
evidence: 844c7100: the arm also requires kind == Renamed. New test copy_from_al_to_non_al_is_not_al gives exactly diff-file-not-al on src/posting.json. Proof: dropping the kind check gives diff-file-deleted src/posting.al. Code-review's CR5 (no test pinned it) is closed by this test.

text: holds_workspace_files missed an Only-in path that is the diff-root/git-top prefix itself or a folder above it (strip_diff_prefix returns None), so `Only in .: Cloud` read as diff-file-not-al. No test covered the folder check under a diff root (opus F3).
evidence: 844c7100: at_or_above_prefix counts the prefix and its parent folders as holding workspace files when the workspace has any key. New test only_in_diff_root_prefix_folder_stays_unmatched, under repo_ws: ./Cloud is unmatched, a sibling folder is not-al, and ./apps (parent of deep/apps/Cloud) is unmatched. Proof: disabling the branch fails it.

text: A both-sides /dev/null record (the parser's 'unknown' placeholder path) became diff-file-not-al unknown instead of diff-file-deleted unknown.
evidence: 844c7100: a Deleted record with no old_path skips the guard. Test dev_null_both_sides_stays_deleted, with a proof.

text: A3(e) rename_from_non_al_to_al_takes_the_new_file had no recorded mutation, though the spec says every A3 case has one.
evidence: 844c7100: the proof classifies on old_path.unwrap_or(path); the test fails (diff-file-not-al, no roots) and passes after the revert. Recorded in the ledger table.

text: The schema contract called 1.8.0 additive although it narrows two kinds, and it omitted the Only-in folder exception to the AL-only meaning of diff-file-unmatched.
evidence: 844c7100: the contract says a minor bump removes or renames no field and may add a field or kind, that 1.8.0 is not purely additive because it narrows two kinds, and it names the Only-in folder exception.

text: The CHANGELOG defined diff-file-unmatched without the Only-in folder exception and said every non-AL file was diff-file-unmatched before (deletions were diff-file-deleted; binary/mode-only sections were never reported).
evidence: 844c7100: the entry now names the exception, the old deletion kind, the unreported sections, copies, the /dev/null placeholder and the diff-root prefix rule.

text: holds_workspace_files scanned every workspace key for each Only-in entry: O(entries × files).
evidence: 844c7100: workspace_folders builds the folder-key set once per run, lazily at the first non-AL Only-in path, and the check is a set lookup. Behaviour is pinned by A3(c) and U2's test.

text: An Only-in folder of AL source that only the old tree has (deleted), or one outside the workspace, is labelled diff-file-not-al, which states something false.
evidence: This is the stated limit both reviewers ratified as T13 (ledger 'Stated limits'). Paths alone cannot tell a deleted AL folder from a non-AL one, and the old tree is not probed because its paths may not exist on disk. The CHANGELOG and the contract state it.

text: The AL classification is two guards in resolve_changed_roots rather than inside diff_key; a future diff-path source must remember its own guard. al_looking is a one-line wrapper.
evidence: This placement was ratified as T12. diff_key cannot hold it because deletions bypass diff_key, and the two guards differ by necessity (renames versus the Only-in folder check). al_looking adapts &str to the shared source_text::has_al_extension(&Path), so it is not a second rule. Both share that one helper.
